Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2584); Anna, an Israelitess:--Anna.
BiblicalUsage: Anna is the prophetess of the tribe of Asher, eighty-four years old, who lived in the temple with fastings and prayers and spoke of the child Jesus to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem. Luke gives her a husband, seven years of marriage, a long widowhood, and a life spent waiting in the temple.
TheologicalSignificance: Anna waited in the temple for decades, and I believe her waiting is the pattern for mine: prayer and fasting in the dark, and then the child in her sight at last. I hold that no long waiting is wasted when it ends in seeing Christ.
RelatedEvents: The Presentation of Jesus in the Temple
